p1.original: 13.1 治疗心理障碍的方法多种多样，但它们都涉及侧重于改善一个人的心理、行为或社会功能的治疗关系。
p1.en: 13.1 The treatment of mental disorders is varied, but they all involve therapeutic relationships focused on improving a person's psychological, behavioural or social functioning.

p2.original: 13.2 心理学家采用的治疗方法主要有两种，即领悟疗法（侧重于发展对自身及其问题的理解）和行为疗法（侧重于通过条件作用来改变行为）。
p2.en: 13.2 There are two main treatments used by psychologists, namely, epithetic therapy (focusing on developing understanding of themselves and their problems) and behavioural therapy (focusing on changing behaviour through conditionality).

p3.original: 13.3 生物医学疗法尝试用药物改变大脑的化学反应，通过手术改变大脑的神经通路，或者通过电脉冲或强磁场改变其活动方式来治疗心理障碍。
p3.en: 13.3 Biomedical therapy attempts to modify the chemical reaction of the brain with drugs, to alter the neuropaths of the brain through surgery, or to treat psychological disorders by changing the mode of activity by electric pulses or powerful magnetic fields.

p4.original: 13.4 尽管心理疗法和医学疗法结合起来治疗精神障碍通常比单独用某一种方法的疗效更好，但对于大多数没有特定“生活问题”的人而言，最好单独接受心理治疗。
p4.en: 13.4 While the combination of psychotherapy and medical therapy is usually more effective than a single method, for the majority of people who do not have a particular “life problem”, it is preferable to receive psychological treatment alone.

p5.original: 德里克感到疲倦和不开心已经断断续续好几个月了，同时，他意识到不仅是工作，他和朋友的关系也因此受到了影响。同事兼朋友米歇尔（Michelle）委婉地建议他去寻求专业帮助，但德里克不确定该去哪里寻求帮助。和许多人的做法一样，他向另一个三年前接受过心理治疗的朋友寻求建议。虽然他的心里有点忐忑，但最终还是来到了施图姆（Sturm）医生的办公室。
p5.en: Derek has been tired and unhappy for months, and at the same time he realizes that not only work, but also that his relationship with friends has been affected. My colleague and friend Michelle had kindly advised him to seek professional help, but Derek was not sure where to go to seek help. Like many others, he sought advice from another friend who had undergone psychological treatment three years earlier. Although he was a little upset, he ended up in the office of Dr. Sturm.

p6.original: 最后，德里克发现，施图姆很容易相处，并且很快他们俩一致认为德里克得了抑郁症。在双方讨论了抑郁症的性质后，施图姆医生说：“我们有几种治疗方法可供选择，我曾接受过认知行为疗法的培训，该疗法将抑郁症视为一类习得性问题，通过改变人们对生活事件和人际关系的看法来进行治疗。如果采用这种方法，我们将探讨在工作和家庭中发生的可能触发抑郁发作的情境。我还会每周给你布置‘家庭作业’，这些作业旨在帮助你发挥自己的优势，而不是只关注自己的不足。就像在学校时一样。”她微笑着补充道。
p6.en: Finally, Derek found that Stum was easy to get along with, and soon they agreed that Derek was depressed. After discussing the nature of depression, Dr. Schtum said: “We have several options for treatment, and I have been trained in cognitive behaviour therapy, which treats depression as a form of acquired sexuality by changing people's perceptions of life events and relationships. If this approach is followed, we will explore the situations that may trigger depression at work and in the home. I'll also set you up weekly "homeworks" designed to help you to take advantage of yourself, not just to focus on your own shortcomings. Just like in school. She smiled and added.

p7.original: “作为第二种选择，我可以将你推荐给采用心理动力疗法的同事。如果你选择这种疗法，将和尤因（Ewing）医生探讨你的过去，找寻可能导致你产生当下感觉的事件。从本质上讲，这种疗法旨在让你的潜意识中某些令人不快的部分暴露在光天化日之下。
p7.en: “As a second option, I can recommend you to colleagues who use psychodynamic therapy. If you choose this therapy, you will discuss your past with Dr. Ewing, looking for events that may give you a sense of the moment. Essentially, this therapy is designed to expose some of the unpleasant parts of your subconscious to daylight.

p8.original: “或者，如果你愿意，我可以将你转给我的朋友基弗（Kiefer）医生，他通常把治疗重心放在患者的目标、人际关系和自尊上。我们称其为人本主义疗法，它更多地处理的是你的有意识的想法，而非潜意识中的内容。
p8.en: “Or, if you like, I can transfer you to my friend, Dr. Kiefer, who usually focuses his treatment on the patient's goals, interpersonal relationships and self-esteem. We call it a humanist therapy, which deals more with your conscious thinking than with subconscious content.

p9.original: “我还可以给你开一些已被证明可以有效治疗抑郁症的药物。它们可能是你曾在杂志和电视广告上看到的某一种抗抑郁药，类似于百忧解（Prozac）。当然，药物发挥作用可能需要几周的时间。并且我不确定它们是否真的能帮助你解决那些让你一直感到沮丧的问题。”
p9.en: "I can also give you some drugs that have been proven to be effective in treating depression. They may be some kind of antidepressant drug that you saw in magazines and television ads, similar to Prozac. Of course, it may take weeks for drugs to work. And I'm not sure if they really help you with the problems that keep you down.

p10.original: 她补充说道：“当然，还有其他一些可供选择的治疗方案，如电抽搐疗法，人们通常称其为‘休克疗法’，但我认为你的情况不需要采用电抽搐疗法。”
p10.en: She added: “Of course, there are other options for treatment, such as electroconvulsive therapy, which is commonly called “shock therapy”, but I do not think your situation requires electroconvulsive therapy.

p11.original: “仅仅是听到这些就让我感觉好一些，”德里克叹了口气说，“所以，我需要选择药物治疗或者心理治疗中的一种？”
p11.en: “Just hearing that makes me feel better,” Derek said, “So I need to choose between medication or psychotherapy?

p12.original: 施图姆医生回答：“或者可以二者联合。”
p12.en: Dr. Schtum replied: “Or we can combine them.

p13.original: “那我该怎么做决定？”德里克问。
p13.en: "What am I supposed to do about it? Derek asked.

p14.en: This chapter considers the following topics:

p15.original: 治疗德里克的抑郁症的最佳方法是心理治疗、药物治疗或二者联合？更广义地说，我们如何决定选择哪一种治疗方法这一问题适用于任何一种精神障碍。
p15.en: The best way to treat Derek's depression is through psychotherapy, medication or a combination of both? More broadly, how we decide which treatment to choose applies to any mental disorder.

p16.original: 尽管施图姆医生和她的同事在工作中采用了不同的治疗方法，但绝大多数接受治疗（therapy）的人都得到了明显的帮助。当然，并不是每个个案的治疗都能成功。有些人的问题拖了太久，已经变得十分棘手；有些人没有针对他们的问题采用恰当的治疗方法。而且，不幸的是，还有许多可以从治疗中受益的人由于治疗费用高昂而无法获得治疗。尽管如此，发展出各种有效的疗法仍然是现代心理学的成果之一。
p16.en: Although Dr. Stum and her colleagues used different treatments in their work, the vast majority of those receiving treatment (the others) received obvious help. Of course, not every case is treated successfully. Some people's problems are too long and have become very difficult; Some do not have appropriate treatments for their problems. Moreover, unfortunately, there are many people who can benefit from treatment who are unable to access it because of its high cost. Nevertheless, the development of effective therapies is still one of the achievements of modern psychology.

p17.original: 当你通读本章时，我们希望你能够权衡每种疗法的优缺点。此外还要记住，有时你的朋友或亲戚会如同德里克那样，让你使用在本章学到的知识给他们推荐适当的治疗方法。甚至有可能某天是你自己需要选择治疗师。但是请记住，本章不会教你如何做心理治疗。
p17.en: When you read this chapter, we hope that you will be able to weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each treatment. It is also important to remember that sometimes your friends or relatives, like Derek, will let you use the knowledge gained in this chapter to recommend appropriate treatments to them. It's possible that one day you'll have to choose a therapist. But remember, this chapter will not teach you how to do therapy.
